To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Nové Mesto and Zabrekh units represent back-arc basin metabasites, formed in an extensional setting, with a boninite-type association of mafic rocks, which formed in the presence of an upwelling hot asthenosphere and a slab window.
the Nové Mĕsto Unit and the northwestern part of the Zabreh Unit comprise back-arch basin mafic volcanic rocks metamorphosed by Variscan tectonism.
the Nové Mesto–Zábrezh association of metabasite rocks represents a back-arc basin magmatism in a subduction zone setting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the petrology, geochemistry and Nd isotope systematics of metabasites from the Nové Mesto Unit and the northern Zábřeh Unit of the Orlica–Śnięznik Dome.
the origin of the Nové-Město–Zábrež Unit metabasites and their significance for the evolution of the Cadomia–Teplá–Bárandia subduction system.
the origin, evolution, and geodynamic significance of the metabasites of Nové Mě sto Unit and northern part the Zábřeh unit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabasites of Nové Městvo and Zábřeh units are products of back-arc basin magmatism, which was induced by the upflow of asthenosphere through a subducted ridge (subduction window).
the Nové Mĕsto Unit represents an oceanic island arc, whereas the Zábřeh unit represents a back-arc basin, both formed in the Cadomian orogeny and metamorphosed during the Variscan orogeny.
the Nové Mĕsto–Zábřeh association of metabasitic rocks represents a fragment of a Cadomian oceanic basin that was subducted in a northwesterly direction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Nové Mesto–Zabrěh Unit is the easternmost Cadomian subducting zone in the Bohemian Massifs.
the Nové Mřesto Unit and northern part Zábřeh Unit are the Cadomian back-arc basin remnants, which were affected by a hot upflow of asthenospheric mantle.
a slab-window-like setting in a subduction zone is a key factor for the formation of boninites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Nové Mesto–Zábřeh metabasites were formed in a back-arc basin setting, and that the boninite-type magmatization was related to the upflow of hot, asthenospheric mantle through a slab window.
